Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have earned acclaim from critics, audiences, and award bodies alike.

|---|-------|----------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | December 25, 2020 (limited) | A masterclass in storytelling and time‑jumps, this epic chronicles the life of hitman Frank Sheeran. Scorsese’s use of de‑scalation and the film’s emotional depth make it a standout crime saga. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | March 27, 2020 | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced humor and intricate plot twists keep viewers guessing. The film’s stylish direction and sharp dialogue make it a modern gangster classic. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | April 24, 2020 | Though more political drama than pure thriller, its courtroom tension and razor‑sharp dialogue deliver a gripping narrative about justice and dissent. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | May 15, 2020 | A psychological thriller that follows a man accused of a crime he didn’t commit. The film’s tense atmosphere and moral ambiguity create a chilling experience. |
| 5 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | June 12, 2020 | A modern take on the classic horror story, this film blends sci‑fi with crime‑thriller elements as a woman fights to prove her abuser’s existence. Its suspenseful pacing and strong female lead earned critical praise. |
| 6 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | July 17, 2020 | A historical crime‑drama that examines truth and justice in medieval France. Scott’s meticulous production design and the film’s moral complexity make it a compelling watch. |

- **Streaming**: Many of these titles are available on major platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, and HBO Max. Check your local listings or streaming services for availability.
